implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — write the goal-specific security assertions before their cases exist. Do not weaken the existing generic roster-versus-arms checks.

ADD REAL BEFORE/AFTER/RACE CASES AND DURABLE PROOFS. In `scheduler-activation-hostile-cases.ts`, import the production GOAL prerequisite/qualification surfaces and reuse the established bootstrap and goal-closure arrangers (`openStore`, `driveThrough`, `send`, `envelope`, `acceptancePayload`, `decisionCount`, `GOAL_ID`, `approveNodes`, `seedReviewAcceptance`, `seedVerifiedNode`) only to create real SQLite facts. Route all three through one capture helper that returns the exact `send(...)` object unchanged while recording before/after raw decision counts, goal event counts, `GoalCompleted` counts, and durable goal result bytes. Export read-only proof accessors/cleanup, prove four actual hostile command outcomes were captured, and close bootstrap stores before cleaning temporary verification roots. No production file or test helper may synthesize the refusal.

GREEN — PIN THE ANSWERING LAYER, ZERO RESIDUE, AND AN ACCEPTED CONTROL. In `scheduler-activation-boundaries.security.ts`, update the measured scheduler-axis cardinality 25→26 and complete the RED assertions. For every GOAL hostile outcome assert the exact code and raw production `refusedBy === GOAL_PREREQUISITE_LAYER` (not merely a projected layer), object identity with the captured service return, unchanged decision/event/result snapshots, and zero `GoalCompleted` admissions. Add one accepted control through the SAME capture/command helper: approve one node, seed its accepted review and one real PASSED verification, submit real `goal.close`, and assert the returned production object is `ok:true`, `disposition:"DECIDED"`, `authority:"DURABLE_DECISION"`; decision count rises by exactly one; exactly one `GoalCompleted` lands; and production readback is lifecycle `COMPLETED`, version 4, with no active graph revision. Assert the GOAL case/control counts are nonzero so generated coverage cannot silently vanish and a refuse-everything implementation cannot pass.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove the assertions remain attached to production. Drill 1 is a transient, never-staged mutation of the completed producer: first require `git status --short -- apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-qualification.ts` empty, record its SHA-256, replace exactly the single `receipt === undefined` refusal guard at the measured range, record the mutant hash, and run the focused scheduler suite; the named BEFORE/RACE exact-code tests must redden on the production behavior. Drill 2 makes one exact reversible edit in the owned hostile-case driver so it returns a literal/copy of the expected refusal instead of the actual `send(...)` object; the named production-object-identity/accepted-control assertion must redden. Restore exact bytes and verify hashes/status. Record the applied range, the intended failing test, and the red output for both drills. These are test mutations only: the final diff and commit remain restricted to the three `tests/security` paths.

planningNotes.risks: The AFTER arm must first demonstrate a genuinely qualified production value before adding the conflicting second receipt; otherwise it is just another initially-invalid fixture. A returned refusal alone cannot prove zero residue, so raw decisions, goal events, completion events, and durable result bytes are compared. Multiple layers can refuse goal.close; assert the raw service `refusedBy`, not only the matrix projection. A refusal-only matrix can pass if the driver always refuses, hence the accepted control through the same driver. The store replay identity could hide duplicated decisions, hence raw counts and distinct command IDs in the race. Real verification fixtures spawn bounded child processes and temporary roots; close stores before cleanup, especially on Windows. The production mutation drill touches an unowned completed path only transiently; hash/status preconditions and inverse restoration are mandatory, and any concurrent change is a hard stop. The full security gate remains red from foreign GRAPH_CONTENT by design; disclose exact output and use the owned-path delta rather than inventing green.
